description.content:
List the co-sell solutions registered with AWS Partner Central for
your account. Solution identifiers are referenced by `solutions` on
opportunities.

Returns the active co-sell solutions registered with AWS Partner Central for the
authenticated vendor.

For vendor accounts provisioned for use in a test environment, this endpoint
returns a fixed three-solution fixture; the `q`, `from`, `pageSize`, and
`all` query parameters are **ignored** for these vendors and the response
body is the same fixture set regardless of what the client sends. Production
vendor accounts receive vendor-specific results that honor every query
parameter.

query.description: A search query to filter the solutions.
The starting index of the solutions to return.
The number of solutions to return per page (minimum 1, maximum 100, default 10).

Set to `true` to return solutions in any status, including inactive ones.
Defaults to `false` (only active solutions are returned).

info.name: Tackle Public Contracts Authentication Solutions API

description.content:
Customer-facing read API for cloud marketplace contracts that Tackle has
ingested for your Tackle account.

The response shape is a stable projection of the underlying
contract document. It is intended to be safe to consume long-term: fields
will be added over time, but documented fields will not be removed without
deprecation notice.

## Authentication

Every request must include a valid Tackle JWT in the `Authorization`
header (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Machine-to-machine (MTM) tokens
issued for your Tackle account are accepted. The token scopes every
response to the account it represents.

## Pagination

`GET /api/contracts` is the only paginated endpoint. Pagination uses an
opaque `cursor` query parameter:

1. The first request omits `cursor`.
2. If more pages exist, the response includes a `next` field. Pass that
   value verbatim back as `cursor` on the next request.
3. The last page omits `next`.

Cursors are opaque tokens. Do not parse, modify, or persist them across
schema changes — request a fresh page from the start instead.
